reasoning: Recent general-election polling for the South Carolina Senate race shows Republicans with a mid-to-high single–digit lead over Democrats, and no credible presidential general-election polling in the last 45 days indicates any different pattern from the state’s strong Republican lean.[1][9] The best available aggregate—Pollsmax’s statewide Senate polling average updated July 8, 2026—has the Republican ahead by 7.4 points, consistent with South Carolina’s R+12 Cook PVI and with prediction-market and analyst expectations that the seat and the state remain clearly Republican-leaning.[1][9] Intraparty GOP primary polls over the past month show a competitive field but do not change the underlying D vs. R balance of the November race.[3][7][8][11]

sources.name: Pollsmax
sources.details: Pollsmax’s 2026 South Carolina Senate polling average shows Republicans at 48.7% vs. 41.3% for Democrats, for a statewide general-election margin of R+7.4.

sources.name: Newsweek (reporting Impact Research)
sources.details: Impact Research poll of 700 likely voters finds appointed Sen. Darline Graham leading Democrat Annie Andrews 48% to 45%, a head-to-head general-election margin of R+3.

sources.name: The Hill (reporting Emerson College Polling/Nexstar)
sources.details: Emerson College/Nexstar poll of 500 likely GOP primary voters shows Ralph Norman at 22% and Darline Graham at 19% in the Republican Senate primary, indicating a competitive Republican field but not directly changing the R vs. D general-election margin.

sources.name: WPDE (reporting Innovative Communication Strategies)
sources.details: Innovative Communication Strategies poll of 788 verified Republican primary voters finds Ralph Norman at 18.6% and Darline Graham at 16.3%, a 2.3-point edge within the margin of error in the GOP Senate primary.

sources.name: Newsmax (reporting Trafalgar Group)
sources.details: Trafalgar Group tracking poll of 989 likely Republican voters shows Darline Graham leading the GOP Senate primary with 27.0%, followed by Russell Fry and Ralph Norman at 17.4% each, highlighting an unsettled Republican field but no D vs. R margin.

sources.name: Newsweek
sources.details: A GOP primary survey reported by Newsweek finds interim Sen. Darline Graham at 20.8% and Ralph Norman at 16.9%, underscoring that the Republican nomination is competitive and likely headed to a runoff, but offering no direct general-election D vs. R margin.

sources.name: The Hill (reporting Emerson College Polling/Nexstar)
sources.details: Earlier Emerson College/Nexstar poll of 500 likely GOP primary voters shows Ralph Norman at 16.4% with high undecided (17.9%), confirming a fragmented Republican field in the special Senate primary.

sources.name: Emerson College Polling/Nexstar
sources.details: Emerson College Polling/Nexstar’s full release on the July 14-15 South Carolina special Senate primary poll finds no clear GOP leader, with Ralph Norman at 16% and Mark Lynch at 13%, reinforcing the lack of a dominant Republican but not altering the underlying partisan lean.
